reason: The crane needs a standing mast before it can be braced.
expectation: The uprights and crosspiece should form a mast on the base.

effect: The mast is now upright on the base, ready for bracing.
reaction: That was a straightforward first assembly.
reason: Diagonal braces should help the upright mast resist sideways bending.
expectation: The braces should stiffen the mast against sideways movement.

effect: The mast now has triangular bracing, which helps prevent its frame from skewing sideways.
reaction: The explanation made the purpose of the diagonal braces clear.
reason: The boom needs a hinge to attach and pivot on the mast.
expectation: The hinge pin should prepare the boom for attachment to the mast.

effect: The boom now has its hinge pin and appears ready to attach to the braced mast.
reason: The prepared boom should attach to the mast at its hinge.

choice.combine: Boom with its captive hinge pin

expectation: The boom should join the braced mast while remaining able to pivot.

effect: The hinged boom is now attached to the braced mast.
reaction: The assembly followed the expected hinge connection.
reason: The boom support stay should hold the hinged boom in position.

choice.with: Crane frame with a hinged boom

expectation: The stay should support the boom on the crane frame.

effect: The stay now supports the hinged boom.
reason: The pulley wheel needs its fork and axle to rotate and mount on the crane.
expectation: The wheel should fit into the fork on its axle.

effect: The pulley is assembled, and I learned that it redirects the pull without reducing the load.
reaction: The distinction between changing direction and reducing weight was useful.
reason: The pulley in its fork should mount at the end of the supported boom.

choice.with: Crane boom held by its stay

expectation: The pulley should attach to the crane boom.

effect: The pulley is now mounted at the boom tip.
reaction: That attachment followed the expected assembly.
reason: The spreading feet should widen the crane's support on the ground.

choice.with: Crane frame with a tip pulley

expectation: The feet should stabilize the crane frame.

effect: The spreading feet widened the crane’s support, and the braced frame completed the goal.
reaction: The final stability test was a satisfying confirmation of the construction.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the diagonal braces was most worthwhile: the explanation showed why triangles resist the sideways distortion of a rectangular frame.

leastWorthwhile.text: Preparing and attaching the boom hinge were straightforward but less revealing than the bracing and pulley explanations.

surprise.text: The fixed pulley changes the direction of the pull without halving the weight; that distinction changed how I understood its job.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the parts had recognizable roles in the crane.

continue.text: Yes. The explanations of bracing and the pulley were useful, and I would be curious to see the crane lift the basket.
